followUps.title: Decide: bound message and label keys before the P0 freeze (ADR-0005)
followUps.body:
`AuditValidationErrorSchema.key` and `params.labelKey` (`packages/core/src/contracts/audit.ts`) and config `Key` (`packages/core/src/config/schema-fields.ts`) are unbounded `z.string().min(1)`. Tightening after the P0 freeze is a breaking audit change.

Options:
1. Bound message and label keys with one shared pattern in `contracts/primitives.ts`, used by config and audit together (test first).
2. Add an ADR-0005 line recording that they stay unbounded (server-generated keys, never user text).

**Done when:** the developer has chosen, and the choice is merged before the P0 gate.

**Source:** PR #38 wave-review minor M3 (carry W4R-M3).

followUps.title: Sensitive paths: list nested biome.json files and .gitignore
followUps.body:
Biome honours nested `biome.json` files (`root: false`) and `vcs.useIgnoreFile: true` skips files matched by `.gitignore`. A PR can add `packages/core/biome.json` or a `.gitignore` line and switch off lint, including the core purity rule, without a sensitive-review artifact.

Fixed in PR #76 (ADR-0007 tiers): replace `biome.json` with `**/biome.json` and add `.gitignore` in `.github/sensitive-paths` (or set `useIgnoreFile: false` and rely on `files.includes`), mirror in CLAUDE.md, and extend the shipped-glob test in `scripts/ci/sensitive-review.test.ts`. PR #76 lists both in `[gate]` and closes this issue.

**Source:** PR #38 wave-review residual RR-M1.

followUps.title: GET /api/v1/config returns only the ClientSiteConfig allowlist
followUps.body:
The route handler must return `toClientSiteConfig(resolved, configHash)`, never the server `SiteConfig`, with a test that `auth`, `retention`, `extends` and `Source.kind`, `server`, `maxConcurrent` are absent from the response.

**Source:** W2 Task 9 carry forward (ledger).

followUps.title: getLocale handler returns 400 validationFailed for a malformed locale
followUps.body:
The route contract declares 400 `validationFailed` (ApiError) for a malformed locale param; 404 stays for a well-formed locale that is not listed. The handler implements both, with tests.

**Source:** Ruling W3-5, PR #35.

followUps.title: Confirm Better Auth user ids fit BoundedIdSchema
followUps.body:
Audit `actor.id` and credential user ids use `BoundedIdSchema` (`/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/`, ADR-0005). If Better Auth issues ids outside that pattern, every audit write fails closed. Configure or verify the id generator, with a test that a created user's id parses.

**Source:** W1 xhigh review, Track A note (Ruling P-1).

followUps.title: Client parsers tolerate unknown WS message types and ApiError fields
followUps.body:
M2 and M3 add WS message types and fields additively. The WS client and the ApiError receipt parser must ignore unknown types and fields instead of failing, with tests.

**Source:** W1 xhigh review M10, Track B note.

followUps.title: promote.yml: milestone argument, full history, fail on non-zero
followUps.body:
When `promote.yml` runs the story-tag gate it passes `--milestone <mN>` as two argv entries, checks out with `fetch-depth: 0` (tags and history), and a non-zero exit fails the job.

**Source:** W4 Task 20 carry forward.

followUps.title: Licence check covers the first runtime dependency of api or apps
followUps.body:
The first task that adds a runtime dependency to `packages/api` or `apps/*` shows it in `pnpm licenses list --prod --json` output, so the CI licence gate really sees workspace runtime dependencies.

**Source:** W4 Task 19 carry forward.

followUps.title: OpenAPI: input-side request bodies and a stable Condition component name
followUps.body:
- `scripts/ci/openapi.ts` emits request bodies (and `WsClientMessage`) with zod `io: "output"`; a body field with a default or transform is published with the wrong required flag or type. Use `io: "input"` for bodies once P1 adds them.
- The recursive `Condition` component is named from zod's internal id (`getConfig200___schema0`) and can change on a zod upgrade, causing spurious drift. Give `Condition` a registry id.

**Source:** W4 Task 17 critic minors M2 and M5.

followUps.title: Threat model: sensitive-review cannot stop a PR editing its own checker
followUps.body:
`sensitive-review` runs on `pull_request`, so a PR can change `ci.yml`, `scripts/ci/sensitive-review.ts` or the lockfile's gate tools and pass without an artifact. Spec 9.1 accepts this (the check proves a review was recorded, and the edit is visible in the diff). Record it in a threat-model doc, and optionally run the base branch's copy of the checker.

**Source:** PR #38 wave-review answer 2.

followUps.title: Core purity lint also catches IO globals
followUps.body:
The Biome override forbids IO imports in `packages/core/src`, but not IO globals that need no import: `fetch`, `process.env`, `WebSocket`, `XMLHttpRequest`. Add a restricted-globals rule for non-test core files, with a probe showing it fires.

**Source:** W4 Task 22 critic minor M3.

followUps.title: Embedded login: validate the host email claim before it reaches audit
followUps.body:
`AuditActor.email` is `z.email().max(254).nullable()`, which rejects host-issued addresses such as `user@cadhost`, IP literals and non-ASCII domains. At `POST /api/v1/auth/embedded`, check the host JWT email claim with `AuditActorSchema.shape.email` and store `null` (or reject the login) when it fails, with a test. Otherwise every audit write, and so every submit (spec 5.2), fails for that principal.

**Source:** PR #38 wave-review minor M2 (carry W4R-M2).

followUps.title: Duplicate response-mapping check uses the canonical when condition
followUps.body:
`checkLimits` keys duplicate response mappings on whether `when` is present, not on the condition itself, so mutually exclusive mappings raise a spurious `duplicateMapping`. Once condition canonicalisation lands, key on the canonical `when`, with a test that distinct conditions pass.

**Source:** W3 Task 13 ruling and carry forward.

followUps.title: Live progress dashboard on GitHub Pages
followUps.body:
The README Mermaid block is regenerated when `scripts/ops/gh-setup-project.mjs` runs. For a live view: a workflow rebuilds an SVG dashboard (milestone progress rings, phase bars from sub-issue progress, the wave timeline, open decisions and follow-ups) on issue and PR events and publishes it to GitHub Pages; the README embeds it.

Needs: Pages enabled (repo admin), a workflow under `.github/workflows/` (sensitive, needs the review artifact), no repository code run next to any token, and a fallback when Pages is down (the Mermaid block stays).

**Source:** Developer request 09-26-26 (README visuals, option both).

followUps.title: Decide: recalibrate review rules before W5 (sdd-task and wave-review by tier)
followUps.body:
ADR-0007 tiered the CI sensitive-review check; our own agent review rules are not tiered yet. PR #76 cost three xhigh reviews (about 1.4M tokens, over 2 hours); W4 cost 74 agents.

Questions to settle before W5:
- `sdd-task`: `sensitive: true` runs Opus medium implementer, fixer, critic, ruler and re-reviewer for every sensitive task. Should gate-tier tasks use ordinary tiers plus the Opus critic, keeping the full set for critical-tier tasks?
- Per-task critic when `wave-review` follows: redundant for gate-tier tasks?
- `wave-review` default effort should follow the PR's highest tier automatically (critical xhigh, gate high), not a manual role override.
- `.claude/workflows/**` and the CLAUDE.md roles table decide how much review everything gets but are in no tier. Gate tier?
- Scope freeze: a PR's sensitive scope is fixed before its review starts; later work goes in the next PR.
- Retro: per role across W1 to W4, which findings were real (spec reviewer, quality reviewer, critic, ruler, checker, re-reviewer).

**Source:** developer, 09-26-26 (after PR #76).

followUps.title: Board tooling: residual minors from the PR #76 review
followUps.body:
Residual minors from the final PR #76 `wave-review` (none fail open):
- [ ] A setup-script rerun forces Done on an open wave parent whose tasks are all closed; derive it from issue state only.
- [ ] The ci job's registry-only lockfile check is a text match; a block-style, quoted or differently spaced `resolution` with a tarball can slip past. Parse `pnpm-lock.yaml` instead.
- [ ] `gh-setup-project.mjs` never rewrites existing issue bodies, so edits to follow-up text (#75) do not reach GitHub.

Note: `scripts/ops/**` and `.github/**` are gate tier (ADR-0007), so these fixes need an Opus high review; bundle them into a wave PR.

**Source:** PR #76 review 3 residual M1, M5, M11.

followUps.title: Roadmap roll-up: milestone parents, Level field, date roll-ups
followUps.body:
The Roadmap view falls apart when tweaked: two layers of data are missing (developer, 09-26-26).

- [ ] Task and follow-up dates: Start = issue created date, Finish = closed date (the roadmap needs custom date fields, so copy them).
- [ ] Parent dates (wave, phase, milestone): Start = earliest child Start; Finish = latest child Finish once all children are closed, else the latest child date so far.
- [ ] Milestone parent issues M0 to M4 (label `epic`), phases as their sub-issues; "No Parent issue" then holds only milestones.
- [ ] `Level` single-select field: Milestone, Phase, Wave, Task, Follow-up. Suggested views: "Plan" (level Milestone, Phase), "P0 detail" (level Wave, Task, grouped by parent).
- [ ] `project-sync` rolls dates up on every event; `scripts/ops/gh-setup-project.mjs` backfills once.
- [ ] README SVG dashboard (option B) reads the same roll-ups.

Gate tier (`.github/workflows/**`, `scripts/ops/**`): ride W5, which gets a gate `wave-review` anyway.

**Source:** Roadmap view feedback, developer 09-26-26.

followUps.title: Track B P1 plan: align with the P0 tokens, platform and shell (W5 phase critic)
followUps.body:
The W5 phase Opus critic (PR #83) found that the Track B P1 plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-25-track-b-p1.md`) contradicts what P0 shipped. Amend the plan before Track B P1 starts:

- [ ] F1 (important): Tasks 1 and 14 still create `packages/client/src/platform.ts` with another shape (`Signal.get`, `WritableSignal`, non-null `tokenStore`, no `clear()`, a `visibility` field; plan lines ~150, 3058, 3114-3116, 5461, 5601). Lead ruling R1: Modify, and use the P0 names (`PlatformSignal.current`, `visible`, nullable `tokenStore`).
- [ ] F4 (important): `styles.css` (plan ~4716-4795) uses variables P0 never emits (`--focus-ring`, `--type-*`, `--space-*`, `--field-required`, `--radius-control`, `--motion-*`), so the focus outline is invalid and no ring shows (spec 6.4). Use the `--qm-` names from `cssVarName` (now including `--qm-focus-ring-width`, `--qm-focus-ring-offset`, `--qm-border-width`, `--qm-color-accent`), drop the literal `48px` (`--qm-target-min`), dedupe `body` and `:focus-visible` with `apps/web/src/shell.css`, and test that no unknown variable is used.
- [ ] F5: Task 12 test expects `:root[data-theme="day"] {`; P0 emits day on bare `:root`.
- [ ] F6: Task 11 quotes stale ratios; `it.each(COLOR_TOKENS)` gets an object (use `Object.keys`).
- [ ] F7: the built entry script has no nonce; under `'strict-dynamic'` the app will not boot unless the API injects one. Use Vite `html.cspNonce` with a placeholder the API replaces, and an e2e check for zero CSP violations (Task 27 dependency).
- [ ] F8: set `document.title` and `<html lang>` from the active locale (NFR-001).
- [ ] F9: reuse P0 `VisuallyHidden` instead of a new `.qm-visually-hidden` class; add `clipPath: "inset(50%)"`.
- [ ] F10: the focus ring colour equals some severity fills; keep offset rings on filled controls and draw badge edges with `color.border`.
- [ ] Shell CSS tests read CSS from disk: a Vite `?raw` CSS import is `""` under Vitest (found in PR #83).

**Source:** W5 phase critic, `.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-25-p0-contracts/w5-phase-critic.md` (Windows ledger), PR #83.

followUps.body:

**Source:** SDD ledger, W5 deferred minors (Tasks 23 to 25, W5A, W5B).

followUps.title: Decide: CI pipeline design before the ruleset (ADR, before W6 Tasks 26 and 28)
followUps.body:
Before the ruleset makes `ci` and `sensitive-review` required (Task 28) and CI grows (Task 26 web build and expo export; Track A P1 image, boot smoke, Playwright, publish), settle the pipeline design so CI never becomes a merge blocker the way the review workflows did on PR #76 (developer, 09-26-26).

- [ ] One stable required check: heavy work in separate jobs, a final `ci` job aggregates them, so new steps never touch the ruleset.
- [ ] Path-scoped jobs: web build, expo export, image and Playwright run only when their paths change (extends the docs-only fast path).
- [ ] Fast fail first: lint and typecheck ahead of parallel heavy jobs; `timeout-minutes` on every job; PR CI budget under 10 minutes.
- [ ] Flake policy: Playwright one retry with trace; quarantine label plus issue; no silent retry loops.
- [ ] External services (oasdiff image, dependency review, pipx zizmor): pinned and cached; an outage fails with a clear message, not a code failure.
- [ ] Break glass: spec 9.1's empty bypass list plus a broken CI deadlocks a CI fix. Who may lift the ruleset (repo admin), when, and how it is logged.
- [ ] Merge style: squash with linear history (spec 9.1) or merge commits for wave PRs, recorded in an ADR.
- [ ] CI duration per PR recorded next to agent metrics.

**Source:** developer, 09-26-26.

followUps.title: Board and repo settings: the manual steps
followUps.body: Views, built-in project workflows and repo settings have no API. Follow the checklist in `docs/project-board.md` (section "Manual steps"), tick it there (it is the one checklist), and close this issue when it is done.

followUps.title: Review cost: split small fixes by tier, board data out of gate, light review for small gate PRs (ADR-0007 amendment, W6)
followUps.body:
Review cost for small gate-tier PRs is out of proportion: #91 (a ReDoS fix plus two small gate edits) pays a full `wave-review` (4 to 5 Opus-high agents, about 0.5M tokens) because `package.json` and `scripts/ops/` are `[gate]` (ADR-0007). Decided by the developer 09-26-26; lands in the W6 PR as an ADR-0007 amendment.

- [ ] **Split small fixes by tier.** An ordinary fix goes in its own PR (CI only). Gate-tier chores ride the next wave PR, which pays for a review anyway. Record it in CLAUDE.md "Controller rules".
- [ ] **Board data out of the gate path.** Move issue numbers, titles, bodies and follow-up data from `scripts/ops/gh-setup-project.mjs` to a data file outside `[gate]` (for example `docs/board/board-data.json`, schema-checked by a test). The script that writes to GitHub stays in `scripts/ops/` (gate). Recording numbers or adding a follow-up becomes an ordinary change.
- [ ] **Light review mode for small gate PRs.** Qualifies: highest tier `[gate]` (never `[critical]`), at most about 50 changed lines in gate paths. One Opus 5.5 agent at effort `medium`, no ruler and no fix pass; findings are fixed inline and the review re-runs; the artifact is written only on approve, front matter `effort: "medium"` plus a light-mode marker. `scripts/ci/sensitive-review.ts` accepts medium only for gate paths and only when it counts the gate-path diff under the limit itself (fails closed on a mislabelled PR). `[critical]` keeps xhigh. Add the mode to `.claude/workflows/wave-review.js` with harness scenarios.
- [ ] ADR-0007 amended (or a superseding ADR); `.claude/workflows/README.md` and CLAUDE.md name the light mode.

Why not Sonnet: gate paths are where a tiny edit switches a check off, and the Opus critic or wave-review caught every fail-open gate the Sonnet reviewers passed (W4: 9 of 9; W5: the lockfile-guard bypass). Changing `sensitive-review.ts` is itself `[critical]`, so the W6 PR takes the xhigh review.

**Source:** developer discussion 09-26-26 after PR #91.

followUps.title: Documentation: final whole-product review, owners for adapters.md and embedding.md, architecture and operations overview (BR-005)
followUps.body:
BR-005 ("Product documentation shall be fully reviewed and updated to reflect the enhancements") is covered only per milestone today: each exit PR refreshes `docs/site-config.md`, `docs/api.md` and `docs/demo.md` (spec 9.5, master plan 4.6). Three gaps, all to fix (developer 09-26-26); items 1 and 3 are handed over with the finished product.

- [ ] **Final whole-product documentation review at M4 exit.** Read the full doc set end to end against the spec and BR-005: consistency, stale sections, cross-links, and whether an admin or site developer can run the product from the docs alone. Run it as a review with an Opus critic over the whole set; fix in the M4 exit PR. Add it to the M4 P3 plan and to master plan 4.6's exit table.
- [ ] **Owners for `docs/adapters.md` and `docs/embedding.md`** (spec 7). Add rows to master plan 4.6's exit-ownership table at the milestones that build them: adapters (SourceAdapter API v1) from the M1 or M2 exit, embedding (6.9 protocol, host JWT) at the M4 exit; refreshed at every later exit.
- [ ] **Architecture and operations overview for a newcomer**, handed over with the finished product: how the pieces fit (core, api, client, web, mobile, config), how a query flows, where audit and credentials live, how to deploy, back up, restore and rotate keys, with links to the runbooks (spec 8.7) and ADRs. Addresses the spec 14 bus-factor risk. Owned by the M4 exit PR; drafted earlier if a phase makes it cheap.

**Source:** developer discussion 09-26-26 (documentation pass).

followUps.title: W6 review minors: CI fail-open edges, board data checks, TokenStore glob case
followUps.body:
Minors from the W6 wave-review (PR #95, `docs/reviews/feat-p0-wave-6.md`), none blocking; each touches a gate or critical file, so they ride the next wave PR (split fixes by tier).

- [x] (done in A1, `feat/a-p1-wave-1` fc9bf64) G-M1 `scripts/ci/changed-paths.mjs`: `docs/board/board-data.json` counts as docs-only, so a board-data-only PR skips `checks` and `test` (the schema test never runs; `loadBoardDataOrExit` still fails closed at run time). Treat `docs/board/**` as non-docs.
- [x] (done in A1, `feat/a-p1-wave-1` fc9bf64) G-M2 `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `web` and `mobile` run only on `outputs.web == 'true'`; a `changes` job that succeeds without emitting the key skips both and the aggregate passes. Invert to `!= 'false'` or have `ci` assert the outputs exist.
- [x] (done in A1, `feat/a-p1-wave-1` fc9bf64) G-M3 `scripts/ops/board-data-schema.mjs`: a follow-up `parent` is not checked against phase and wave numbers; a bad parent throws mid `--apply` after earlier writes.
- [x] (done in A1, `feat/a-p1-wave-1` fc9bf64) G-M4 `scripts/ops/gh-setup-project.mjs`: a follow-up number can point at any live issue the data does not otherwise claim; `--apply` would rename and rewrite it. Consider refusing to adopt an issue whose live labels lack `follow-up`.
- [x] (done in A1, `feat/a-p1-wave-1` c9f6d60) G-M5 `scripts/ci/core-purity.ts`: misses destructuring (`const { fetch } = globalThis`), chained globals (`globalThis.window.fetch`) and aliases.
- [x] (done in A1, `feat/a-p1-wave-1` fc9bf64) G-M6 `.github/dependabot.yml`: no ignore rule for `@types/node` majors above 24 (ADR-0001, plan amendment M5).
- [x] (done in A1, `feat/a-p1-wave-1` fc9bf64) C-M1 `.github/sensitive-paths` (critical): TokenStore globs are case-sensitive kebab-case; `SecureTokenStore.ts` or `tokenStore.ts` would be ordinary. Add a case-insensitive form.
- [x] (done in A1, `feat/a-p1-wave-1` fc9bf64) C-M2 `scripts/ci/changed-paths.mjs`: `git diff --name-only` without `-z` C-quotes non-ASCII paths, so such a path under `apps/web/` or `apps/mobile/` skips its job.
- [x] (done in A1, `feat/a-p1-wave-1` fc9bf64) Declined item: `sensitive-review.ts` exits 2 on a legal branch name with `+`, `@`, `#` or non-ASCII even when no sensitive path is touched; fall back to the `pr-<n>` key instead.
- [x] (docs/open-m0-p1) Track B P1 plan still lists `Delete: apps/web/src/App.tsx` (P0 shipped `shell.tsx`); fix before Track B P1 starts.
- [x] Moved to #171. Tech debt (oasdiff, PR #95): the `api-breaking` label was used to skip a false positive (the #69 rename `getConfig200___schema0` to `Condition`, byte-identical otherwise). The label skips the whole oasdiff step, so a real break in the same PR would pass unseen. Add a rename-aware step (normalise component names, or prove rename-only equivalence against the base) so a component rename never needs the label; and make M0 release notes treat #95 as not breaking.
- [x] (done in B1, `feat/b-p1-wave-1` commit 2da6ea3) Windows-only timeout (Track B, 09-27-26): `scripts/ci/sensitive-review.test.ts` > "deps demotion against a real git repo (C1, I1 repros) > classifies every swap and injection repro as gate, with the sensitive label" runs on vitest's default 5000 ms timeout and takes about 6 s on the Windows machine (slower git process spawns), so `pnpm verify` fails there. Passes on Linux and in CI. Proposed: an explicit per-test timeout of 30000 ms (about 2 lines).

**Source:** W6 wave-review 09-27-26 and the #84 plan amendment.

followUps.title: P0 phase review: audit and WS contract tightenings before the first writer
followUps.body:
Minors from the M0 P0 whole-phase review (gate Step 8, Opus 5.5 high over the 8 P0 critical-tier files; artifact `docs/reviews/docs-status-a-20260927.md`). None blocks the freeze. Contract changes go through master plan 8 (contract change procedure); all are critical tier.

**Land early in P1, before the first audit writer (M1 P2 T1), while no audit rows exist:**
- [x] (#103) C-M1 `packages/core/src/contracts/audit.ts:204,130,148`: envelope `credentialUserId` is unconstrained against `details.credentialOwnerUserId` on `sourceDispatched` and `sourceResponded`; one append-only row can name two credential owners, and owner searches on `audit_event(credential_user_id, at)` can miss delegated queries (SEC-011). Require equality in `AuditEventSchema.superRefine`, with tests.
- [x] (#103) C-M3 `audit.ts:140-146`: `sourceResponded.status` is a hand-written literal list; derive it with `SourceStatusSchema.exclude(["pending", "interrupted"])` (same JSON) and test that every other terminal status is accepted, so a new SourceStatus value cannot crash the dispatcher's audit write.
- [x] (#103) C-M5 `primitives.ts:21-22,44-45`: `BOUNDED_ID_MAX_LENGTH` and `HOST_SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH` are repeated as literals in the regexes; build the patterns from the constants or test the boundary.
- [x] (#103) C-M7 `.github/sensitive-paths`: `packages/core/src/contracts/version.ts` (WS protocol version) and `packages/core/contracts/ws-events.schema.json` are ordinary tier; list them under [critical] (query dispatch).

**Before M4:**
- [ ] C-M2 `audit.ts:263-270`: a row with `identitySource: "host"` and no `hostSubject` passes; spec 5.6 requires the host subject on host rows (SEC-010). Require it, with a test.
- [ ] C-M4 `ws.ts:136-185`: strict server-to-client messages in a closed union mean additive WS changes (M2 resultHidden, resync; M3 delegationChanged) break a lagging native client. Decide a client receipt policy (drop unknown types, strip unknown keys) or bump `MIN_CLIENT_VERSION` per additive change; record it through master plan 8.

**With the Track A P1 audit writer (from the feat/core-98 review, M1):**
- [ ] C-M8 `audit.ts`: envelope `credentialUserId` stays unconstrained on `submitted`, `acknowledged`, `interrupted` and `partSkipped`; owner searches on `audit_event(credential_user_id, at)` could over- or under-match. Decide whether `interrupted` copies the `source_result` owner and whether the other query types must omit `credentialUserId`; add the refinement with parse and reject tests (master plan 8).

**Track A (no contract change):**
- [ ] C-M6 `audit.ts:192`: `AuditActor.email` uses `z.email()`; the identity layer may accept addresses that fail it, and an audit write failure fails every submit. IdentityService normalises with `AuditActorSchema.shape.email` and stores null on failure, with a test.

Declined by the reviewer for the developer: whether `packages/api/src/auth/**` should be critical tier (CLAUDE.md does not list authentication as a sensitive area).

**Source:** M0 P0 gate whole-phase review, 09-27-26.
